messages.author: 094f0b846abb8df4
messages.subject: cast(x, a ~ b ~ ., aggregate.fun=mean) does not aggregate correctly?
parts:
Hi all,

I want to aggregate a 2x2x2 array into a 2x2x1 array.

------
> mdat <- melt(array(rnorm(8), dim=c(2,2,2),
dimnames=list(strain=c("s1", "s2"),
treatment=c("t1", "t2"),
gene=c("g1", "g2"))))
> mdat
strain treatment gene value
1 s1 t1 g1 -0.39282103
2 s2 t1 g1 -1.36823389
3 s1 t2 g1 0.60153033
4 s2 t2 g1 -0.07080973
5 s1 t1 g2 -1.05012093
6 s2 t1 g2 0.31942129

> cast(mdat, treatment ~ gene, fun.aggregate=mean) # this should be the result although as 2x2x1 array.
treatment g1 g2
1 t1 -0.8805275 -0.3653498
2 t2 0.2653603 -0.6248085

> cast(mdat, treatment ~ gene ~ ., fun.aggregate=mean) # this goes wrong
, , = (all)

gene
treatment g1 g2
t1 -0.8805275 -0.8805275
t2 -0.3653498 -0.3653498
-----

The first cast() uses a single tilde and returns a data.frame with the
correct values.

The second cast() above, however, only returns the averages for the
fields (t1, g1) and (t1, g2) and these twice. I am not sure: Is this a
bug or do I miss something?

Thanks in advance for you help!

Philip

messages.author: 8757f45da80a9e6c
messages.subject: Re: cast(x, a ~ b ~ ., aggregate.fun=mean) does not aggregate correctly?
parts:
Hi Hadley,

I was looking for reasons to choose between reshape and reshape2 and came across your posting (below) that reshape is basically deprecated.  That's a pretty clear statement, so I'll use reshape2.  However, the most obvious online information isn't so clear.  Your home page points to reshape and doesn't mention reshape2. The Rstudio projects page likewise points to reshape and doesn't mention reshape2. The CRAN entry for reshape doesn't say it is deprecated and doesn't mention reshape2. The CRAN entry for reshape2 says it is a "reboot" of reshape, but doesn't say reshape is deprecated.

I think it would help new users if your personal pages were updated to point to reshape2 and all personal and CRAN pages for reshape and rshape2 state explicitly that reshape is deprecated but kept for the convenience of people with existing reshape code.

Cheers

Ross

On Tuesday, 23 August 2011 16:52:58 UTC+10, Hadley Wickham wrote:
Reshape is basically deprecated - I don't understand the code and it
has no tests so it's basically impossible to fix any bugs without
accidentally creating more.

Hadley
